items.title: Norman Simmons interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 27, 2007 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Levy, his manager, is the one who literally hired me.

ctx.x: You might call it a false start. Actually I was with Carmen’s group at the time. And being in Carmen’s group and who she was and her image, a lot of people had the assumption that for me to play with her and handle her music and I was even writing a lot of it, that again was one of those situations where they kind of blew my image up. So at this particular time, and Carmen was very frugal — well Carmen’s reputation was that she still was not making a lot of money so she didn’t pay a lot of money. But she had a…

Levy, his manager, is the one who literally hired me. Because he said well you know you’ve got to stop running around the country all by yourself hiring different musicians, you need to have a musical director. Because he loved going out and rehearsing the bands himself. Joe loved, yeah, he loved conducting the orchestra and that’s why he could deal with all that himself, and he enjoyed it. But John said that’s not good for your image, you know what I mean, to be going around and sometimes ups and downs. Because…

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: This is how we hit upon a group with Norman Simmons, Sweets Edison, and different people that he put together for his group.

ctx.x: What was he doing then? What was . . .?

He was playing clubs and concerts and doing engagements and had a group. He had a group that he was working with. And a lot of times Joe would do things on his own. When I mean on his own, he would just go into a city and work with a local group. He did that for a while. I kept trying to discourage him from that. You need to get a group together where you’ve got to work with. When I met him – first met him – he would work anywhere, all over the country. He’d work with this one or that one or the other one. I…
Did he – he had his own group in the ’80s?

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: we just take his own, Norman Simmons, his pianist, and then work within the context of the Basie band.

ctx.x: So we kept working with the Basie band and that exists until today. We still work maybe two and three and sometimes as many as four different times a year with the Basie band. And what we do then, we just take his own, Norman Simmons, his pianist, and then work within the context of the Basie band. And we do quite a few of those things. In fact we’re going to be going to play the Montreal festival this year, Toronto festival this year, back to back with the Basie band. And we’ve got an offer on the table now to…
That’s a major project I guess.
